entries.name: Claude Agent SDK for TypeScript
entries.reason: Anthropic presents the Python and TypeScript libraries as language bindings for one Claude Agent SDK product; the Atlas represents that product through the canonical Python repository rather than duplicating the same operational system.
entries.useful_lesson: Language bindings can differ in implementation visibility and license terms even when they expose one product boundary.

entries.name: Google ADK for Go
entries.reason: Google presents Go, Python, TypeScript, Java, and Kotlin implementations as one Agent Development Kit; the Atlas represents the product through the canonical Python repository rather than scoring language bindings separately.
entries.useful_lesson: Cross-language framework parity, test-support licensing, and provider integration depth should be reviewed without multiplying product records.

entries.name: LangSmith
entries.reason: The reviewed repository is a client SDK for tracing and evaluation; it does not itself provide a memory system or a tool-acting agent runtime.
entries.useful_lesson: Agent tracing, evaluation, production observability, and recovery-oriented operations.

entries.name: SQL Chat
entries.reason: The reviewed implementation is a chat-based SQL client that generates and executes user-selected statements, but it does not own an iterative planning, validation, or repair loop required by the data-analysis agent role.
entries.useful_lesson: Conversational database UX, locally stored connection data, self-hosting, and explicit query execution.

entries.name: Gorgias Cortex
entries.reason: Gorgias describes Cortex as its flagship internal AI agent for Gorgias employees rather than a deployable or directly purchasable system available to Atlas users. The public Gorgias AI Agent is a separate customer-facing ecommerce product and is not substituted for Cortex.
entries.useful_lesson: Internal agents can demonstrate cross-application work, employee adoption, and operational patterns without establishing a public product boundary.

entries.name: Hugging Face Text Generation Inference
entries.reason: The repository is archived, so the runtime no longer represents an operational choice a reader could adopt. Hugging Face Inference Endpoints remains separately represented as a managed inference service, and that service boundary is not substituted for the archived runtime.
entries.useful_lesson: Production serving engines can reach end of life while the managed service built on them continues; collection boundaries should be checked against repository lifecycle, not brand continuity.

entries.name: llamafile
entries.reason: llamafile packages llama.cpp and model weights into one portable executable. Its own documentation states it relies on llama.cpp for serving and inherits that project's server interface and endpoints, and the repository pins the upstream commit rather than forking it. What it adds is a distribution format, not a separate execution boundary, so the published llama.cpp record already represents the runtime. No local-runtime type fits it either: it manages no model store, and nothing embeds it because it embeds the weights.
entries.useful_lesson: A packaging innovation can be genuinely valuable without being a distinct operational boundary; check whether the candidate serves models itself or delegates to a runtime already represented.
